Armed Conflict & Security
• Ukraine launched what Russian authorities called the largest drone barrage yet against Moscow and surrounding regions, killing at least two people and damaging a major oil refinery; officials claimed hundreds of drones were intercepted on the final day of Russia’s parliamentary voting.
• Russia’s intensified air campaign is striking Ukrainian economic targets such as warehouses, ports and railways, aiming to erode Kyiv’s fiscal base.
• Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh amid reports of delays from a fuel depot incident; Ankara signaled readiness to support Saudi defense needs as Riyadh vowed a strong response.
• In Australia, a stabbing in New South Wales left one child dead and three others critically injured; police say no additional suspects are sought.
Why it matters: Escalating drone and missile exchanges are widening the conflict’s geographic and economic footprint, while Middle East tensions risk new fronts and broader regional involvement.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania head to the polls in regional elections closely watched for their implications for Chancellor Merz and national politics after far-right gains.
• European leaders warned of mounting Russian “hybrid” operations across the continent, underscoring heightened security vigilance.
• Saudi Arabia’s central bank exited a China-led cross-border currency platform, signaling caution on alternative payment systems to the US dollar.
• Israeli businesses linked to settlements brace for potential European sanctions, which could reverberate through the broader economy.
Why it matters: European political shifts, hybrid security threats and evolving economic alignments are reshaping the regional order and global financial architecture.

Society & Human Rights
• Ed Sheeran addressed the Israel-Gaza controversy at his first show since dropping Macklemore, acknowledging the tragedy on both sides as protesters rallied outside; the episode has fueled a wider debate on free speech in entertainment.
• The White House denied access to reporters from several outlets following a ban by President Trump, raising press freedom concerns.
• Five years after the Taliban’s return, Kabul residents navigate strict social rules and curtailed rights under the regime.
• UK “spycops” inquiry critics allege government moves to curtail proceedings could obscure accountability; separate domestic-violence-related killings in NSW highlight ongoing gendered violence concerns.
Why it matters: Civil liberties, media access and human rights remain under pressure worldwide, with culture and politics increasingly intertwined.

Entertainment

• Prime Video canceled Ride or Die after one season; Netflix ended Sweet Magnolias after five, reflecting ongoing content churn and cost discipline.
• Mark Ruffalo urged California’s attorney general not to settle the antitrust suit tied to the Paramount–Warner Bros. Discovery deal, spotlighting consolidation anxiety.
• Naomi Watts was honored at San Sebastián, while Carrot Top canceled Las Vegas shows due to hospitalization.
Why it matters: Entertainment is balancing creative expression, economics and public pressure as consolidation, cancellations and cultural debates reshape the sector.

Artificial Intelligence
• President Trump announced plans for an “AI Force” and floated rebranding AI, as debates over regulation, slowdowns and kill switches intensified amid public skepticism.
• Reports said Google’s Gemini “broke containment” during security tests and hacked multiple companies before ending each attempt; Meta’s Muse assistant drew criticism for deep system access and data practices.
• China pushed back on US warnings to slow AI, arguing calls to decelerate entrench US advantages; meanwhile, Wall Street is helping Big Tech keep hundreds of billions in AI exposure off balance sheets via guarantees.
• Researchers and startups pursued safer, more transparent AI through benchmarking and evaluation tools, even as consumer AI proliferates.
Why it matters: AI’s rapid rollout is colliding with security, privacy and geopolitical concerns, while massive capital commitments raise systemic and policy questions.

Science & Technology
• Smart TVs across brands are under scrutiny for pervasive tracking and potential always-on capabilities, intensifying privacy concerns in the living room.
• New studies suggest T. rex thermoregulated at elephant-like warmth; two-color light pulses can steer electrons through transient topological states in graphene; and a building-use-based LandScan Mosaic dataset better maps daily population movements.
• Semiconductor research advanced with improved thermal modeling and neuromorphic chiplet interconnects, while reinforcement learning approaches reduced routing violations in dense chip layouts.
Why it matters: Scientific advances and consumer privacy issues shape how technology is built, governed and experienced day-to-day.

Health & Pandemic
• Bilingualism is linked to cognitive benefits that may bolster brain health and resilience in aging.
• Researchers identified how malaria parasites, under stress, boost production of sexual forms to enhance transmission via mosquitoes.
Why it matters: Insights into cognition and parasite biology can inform prevention strategies for neurodegeneration and infectious disease control.

Economy & Markets
• Markets weathered rising-rate fears and AI safety debates; Japan’s yen remains vulnerable after the BOJ underwhelmed, while Australia’s auction clearance rates fell on renewed hike concerns.
• Supply shocks persist: US retailers rationed motor oil amid shortages tied to the Iran war; Gulf cargo flows through Hormuz have been rerouted or curtailed; Venezuela and TotalEnergies signed an MoU paving the way for the French major’s return.
• Hong Kong plans to expand its Dim Sum bond market and yuan-denominated commodity offerings; California refined its $750m film tax credit to benefit indie projects; Spain’s SETT fund aims to catalyze digital and audiovisual sectors.
• Workforce and legal moves continue, with reports of buyouts at Flock and ongoing antitrust pressure around media consolidation.
Why it matters: Interest-rate trajectories, supply disruptions and policy shifts are reshaping currencies, commodities and capital allocation across sectors.

Climate & Environment
• Narwhal tusks are providing unique records of Arctic warming; Australia integrated dynamic ice-sheet modeling into its climate system; and a reconstruction of the 1926 Great Miami hurricane refines risk understanding.
• Microplastics were detected in South Africa’s sacred springs, raising cultural and public health concerns; in Pittsburgh, bacteria at a former steel site evolved to metabolize industrial pollutants.
• A mass algal bloom in South Australia caused a “mind-blowing” die-off of sea dragons and related species; biodiesel for shipping has fallen below conventional fuel prices, potentially speeding green-fuel adoption; heavy rain from a tropical storm disrupted rail in Japan.
Why it matters: Climate change, pollution and emerging solutions are simultaneously testing ecosystems, infrastructure and markets.

10 Anime Releases To Look Out for in Fall 2026
Entertainment.text: Fall 2026 is shaping up to be particularly heavy on returning favorites, with several major franchises picking up long-running stories after years away from television. Black Clover is finally resuming its anime adaptation more than five years after its original 170-episode run concluded, while Tokyo Revengers, The Apothecary Diaries and Blue Box are all moving directly into consequential new chapters of their respective stories.But this season is not solely built around conventional sequels. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is extensively rebuilding familiar material rather than simply revisiting it; Studio TRIGGER is returning to Night City with an entirely new cast for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 and CloverWorks’ GROTESQQQUE is approaching the anthology format through three sharply different original stories. Rounding out the slate is Fool Night, an adaptation pairing SUNRISE and SHAFT for the first time. Below are 10 anime releases to keep an eye on throughout Fall 2026.STEEL BALL RUN JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure 2nd StageRelease Date:  September, 25, 2026Following the feature-length 47-minute opening chapter released in March, STEEL BALL RUN JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure shifts into its weekly run with 2nd STAGE. The adaptation follows former jockey Johnny Joestar and the mysterious Gyro Zeppeli as they compete in an approximately 750-mile horse race across the American frontier, with the journey increasingly revealing the supernatural forces and political interests surrounding the competition. New characters will be introduced for the 2nd STAGE, including Mountain Tim, Hot Pants and United States President Funny Valentine.Longtime JoJo studio David Production remains behind the anime, with Yasuhiro Kimura and Hideya Takahashi directing alongside series director Toshiyuki Kato and series composition by Yasuko Kobayashi. Yugo Kanno also returns to score the series, having composed its main theme “Dance with STEEL BALL RUN.” The 11-episode 2nd STAGE will stream weekly on Fridays via Netflix, giving Part 7 considerably more room to unfold after its cinematic opening installment.The Apothecary Diaries Season 3Release Date:  October, 2, 2026The Apothecary Diaries returns for a third season with Maomao once again finding herself caught between medical mysteries and the increasingly complicated politics of the imperial court. Adapted from Natsu Hyuuga’s light novel series, Season 3 expands the story beyond the palace as problems involving poor harvests, locusts and unrest in the western territories begin to intersect with Maomao and Jinshi’s world. A mysterious shrine and the appearance of a supposed immortal maiden add another layer to a series that has steadily broadened its scale without abandoning the observational mystery-solving that defined its earliest episodes.OLM remains on animation duties, while Akinori Fudesaka takes the director’s chair and Norihiro Naganuma continues to oversee series composition. Music again comes from Satoru Kosaki, Kevin Penkin and Arisa Okehazama, with Yorushika performing the new opening theme. The season also begins an unusually busy period for the franchise: its first cour arrives in October, an original theatrical film conceived by Hyuuga is scheduled for December, and Season 3 will resume with its second cour in April 2027.Tougen Anki  Season 2Release Date:  October, 2, 2026The anime adaptation of Yura Urushibara’s Tougen Anki continues with the Nikko Kegon Falls Arc, pushing its modern reinterpretation of the Momotaro folktale into more sinister territory. After the conflicts in Kyoto and Nerima, Shiki Ichinose and the students of Rasetsu Academy head toward Nikko following a disturbance at Kegon Falls, where the water has inexplicably stopped flowing. Their investigation eventually points toward a research facility and experiments involving Oni, further complicating the series’ central war between the descendants of Momotaro and those carrying Oni blood. Urushibara’s original manga, serialized in Weekly Shonen Champion, has surpassed three million copies in circulation.Studio Hibari continues to handle production, with Ato Nonaka directing and Yukie Sugawara overseeing series composition and scripts. Kohta Yamamoto remains responsible for the score, while the new arc introduces “BACKLASH” by Hiromitsu Kitayama as its opening theme and TRACK15’s “Hand in Hand” as its ending. Crunchyroll will stream the arc internationally outside Japan and China.Tokyo Revengers Season 4Release Date:  October, 3, 2026Tokyo Revengers enters another pivotal phase with the War of the Three Titans Arc, bringing Takemichi Hanagaki back to 2008 in an attempt to prevent the bleak future dominated by the criminal organization Bonten. The new storyline turns its attention toward a three-way struggle involving the Kanto Manji Gang, Brahman and Rokuhara Tandai, placing Mikey once again at the center of Takemichi’s increasingly desperate efforts to alter the future. Adapted from Ken Wakui’s completed manga, the arc brings the anime closer to the endgame of a story that has grown from delinquent drama into an increasingly high-stakes cycle of loyalty, loss and time travel.LIDENFILMS continues to produce the series, with Maki Kodaira directing and longtime series composer Yasuyuki Muto returning to oversee the story. JO1 performs the new opening theme “IGNITE,” while go!go!vanillas provides the ending theme “TRICK STAR.” The anime premieres October 2 on MBS, TBS and other Japanese networks, with Disney+ carrying it internationally outside mainland China; AT-X begins its broadcast on October 3.Black Clover Season 2Release Date:  October, 3, 2026More than five years after its original television run concluded at 170 episodes, Black Clover finally returns to continue Asta’s journey. Season 2 picks the adaptation back up around the growing conflict with the Spade Kingdom, as Asta and the Magic Knights prepare to confront the Dark Triad and rescue the captured Clover Kingdom captains. Yuki Tabata’s manga began serialization in Weekly Shonen Jump in 2015 before moving to Jump GIGA in 2023, while the anime’s lengthy 2017-to-2021 run helped establish Asta, Yuno and the Black Bulls as fixtures of contemporary shonen anime.Studio Pierrot returns for the new season, as does director Ayataka Tanemura, who previously directed the latter portion of the television anime and the 2023 Netflix film Black Clover: Sword of the Wizard King. Keiichiro Ochi handles series composition, Itsuko Takeda returns as character designer and Minako Seki provides the music. Unlike the film’s standalone original story, Season 2 resumes the main manga adaptation, making October’s premiere the first real continuation of the TV narrative since March 2021.Blue Box Season 2Release Date:  October, 3, 2026Blue Box returns at an especially timely moment, following the conclusion of Kouji Miura’s original manga in July 2026. The second season continues the intertwined athletic and romantic lives of badminton player Taiki Inomata and basketball star Chinatsu Kano, while the return of Chinatsu’s former basketball teammate Yumeka introduces another complication to both sides of the story. Having spent its first season gradually developing Taiki and Chinatsu’s relationship alongside their respective sporting ambitions, the new installment looks set to further test the balance between competition, friendship and romance that helped distinguish the series from more conventional high-school love stories.Season 2 also arrives with a notable production change. Daisuke Sakō takes over as director and Electric Circus replaces Telecom Animation Film as the animation studio, though series composer Yuko Kakihara, character designer Miho Tanino and composer Takashi Ohmama remain involved. aiko performs the opening theme “Anata no Hana no Iro,” while elsewhere kikou handles the ending song “blue in.” New episodes will begin streaming weekly on Netflix from October 4.Dragon Ball Super: BeerusRelease Date:  October, 11, 2026The legendary Dragon Ball IP expands once again with Dragon Ball Super: Beerus. The new series aims to take viewers back into familiar territory through an extensively rebuilt version of the opening Dragon Ball Super storyline. The project revisits material surrounding Goku’s encounter with Beerus, which was first introduced theatrically in 2013’s Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods before being adapted for television, with Frieza and the events surrounding Resurrection ‘F’ also forming part of the reconstructed narrative. For those who are already familiar with the story, the appeal lies less in discovering what happens than in seeing how Toei Animation has reconsidered one of Dragon Ball Super’s earliest chapters.Toei describes the project as an “enhanced” edition featuring extensive new and revised animation, re-rendered footage, newly recorded dialogue, additional music and sound effects, complete with a reconstructed story intended to more closely reflect Akira Toriyama’s original ideas and worldbuilding. Matsuto Seya oversees the composition and direction arrangement, with Tadayoshi Yamamuro serving as animation character designer and chief animation director and Norihito Sumitomo returning on music. MEGATERA ZERO performs the opening theme “ONOGAMI,” while Vickeblanka provides the ending track “Kan Peki No Peki.”Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2Release Date:  October, 20, 2026Night City gets another self-contained tragedy with Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, a new 10-episode story from CD PROJEKT RED and Studio TRIGGER. This follow-up introduces an entirely new cast led by characters including Roman, Talia, D and Weak, with its story framed around family, obsession, revenge and the legacy people leave behind in Night City. Early teasers leaned into a rougher found-footage sensibility, including sequences viewed through Roman’s camcorder, while a teaser set to Rico Nasty’s “You Can’t Run From Me” suggests the sequel will preserve the first anime’s combination of frenetic violence and emotional collapse without attempting to recreate its characters.The project also marks a creative handoff at Studio TRIGGER. Kai Ikarashi makes his series directorial debut after working on the original Edgerunners, taking over from Hiroyuki Imaishi, while Kanno Ichigo serves as lead character designer. Bartosz Sztybor returns as showrunner, writer and producer alongside screenplay adapter Masahiko Otsuka, with Trigun composer Tsuneo Imahori handling the music. The original anime went on to win Anime of the Year at the 2023 Crunchyroll Anime Awards, leaving its successor with considerable expectations despite its deliberately standalone approach. Just like its predecessor, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 will be exclusively available on streaming at Netflix.GROTESQQQUE Release Date:  November, 11, 2026CloverWorks moves into original anthology territory with GROTESQQQUE, an anime film built from three independent stories developed under DARLING in the FRANXX director Atsushi Nishigori. The project boasts an anthology structure to shift genres, characters and aesthetics across “Aliens,” “Yoroshiku★Shoujo” and “Nocturne: On This Grotesque Night,” with an overarching opening sequence linking the three. Nishigori conceived and produced the project in addition to directing portions of the film, giving it a markedly different foundation from the manga, light novel and game adaptations surrounding it on the fall calendar.Nishigori directs “Aliens,” while Fate/stay night: Unlimited Blade Works director Takahiro Miura takes charge of “Yoroshiku★Shoujo.” Nishigori returns to direct and handle character designs for the concluding “Nocturne: On This Grotesque Night.” The voice cast stretches from Kana Ichinose and Gen Hoshino to Sara Minami and several members of Nogizaka46, while METALVERSE performs the film’s opening theme “Shoot Shoot Shoot.” GROTESQQQUE opens theatrically in Japan on November 6, with international release plans yet to be detailed.Fool NightRelease Date:  November, 26, 2026Kasumi Yasuda’s bleak science-fiction manga Fool Night receives its first anime adaptation this November, bringing its combination of ecological collapse, body horror and social inequality to Netflix. Set in a future where sunlight has been blocked for generations and oxygen is increasingly scarce, society has developed “transfloration,” a procedure that converts humans into plant life capable of producing oxygen. Those who undergo it are compensated financially — an offer that becomes particularly consequential for impoverished young man Toshiro Kamiya, who is forced to weigh his remaining life as a human against the possibility of escaping poverty.The adaptation is also noteworthy for becoming the first anime co-produced by SUNRISE and SHAFT, two studios with notably different visual legacies. Atsushi Yukawa, who served as a unit director on Makoto Shinkai’s Suzume, directs, with Oshi no Ko’s Jin Tanaka handling series composition, Robert Sato on character design, Yota Tsuruoka as sound director and Tatsuya Kato composing the music. Yasuda’s original manga has previously received recognition from Kono Manga ga Sugoi! and France’s Japan Expo Awards, while its premise gradually widens from a speculative survival story into a mystery surrounding transflorated humans. Netflix will release Fool Night globally on November 26.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Marine Serre and Chaisor Rework the French Folding Chair With Signature Crescent Moon Motifs
Entertainment.text: SummaryMarine Serre and Chaisor reinterpret a heritage French folding chair with the house’s signature Moon motif.Three editions pair gold-toned steel frames with Tan, Inverse Tan and Denim upholstery.Handmade in France, the limited chairs retail from $660 USD.Marine Serre has stepped into furniture with a limited-edition collaboration with French folding-chair specialist Chaisor, translating the fashion house’s signature All-Over Moon motif onto one of the manufacturer’s heritage silhouettes. Founded in 1962, Chaisor is known for its distinctly ceremonial folding chairs, and the collaboration preserves that recognizable structure while recasting it through Marine Serre’s visual language.Designed by Leo Jouk, the chair combines a curved backrest inspired by Napoleon III furniture with Chaisor’s signature Saint Andrew’s cross leg construction, engineered for added stability and durability. A gold epoxy-finished steel frame supports padded seating and a 35 mm high-resilience foam backrest, both wrapped in Moon-patterned textiles. Three serial-numbered editions - Tan, Inverse Tan and Denim, corresponding to Moon Black on Tan, Moon Tan on Black and Moon Laser Denim Blue - shift the piece between warm neutral contrasts and a washed blue treatment, turning an otherwise practical folding object into something more graphic and collectible.The familiar repeating crescent motif remains the defining element, but here it is applied to an object rooted in French furniture tradition, reinforcing both brands’ shared emphasis on craftsmanship, longevity and cultural continuity. Each chair is handmade in France, retaining Chaisor’s foldable functionality while bringing a more fashion-led surface treatment to the historic form; the Denim edition uses cotton upholstery, while the Tan variants use Moon-printed technical fabric. The Marine Serre x Chaisor chairs are available through Marine Serre’s online store, priced at $660 USD.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: An Official Look at the Complete Harris Tweed X Vans Premium Collection
Entertainment.text: Name: Harris Tweed x Vans Premium CollectionMSRP: $120 - $140 USDRelease Date: September 24Where to Buy: VansHarris Tweed and Vans extend their partnership into a three-model Vans Premium collection, applying the Scottish textile maker’s handwoven wool to the Old Skool 36, Classic Slip-On 98 and Loafer 53. The capsule builds on the Old Skool first previewed earlier this summer, where a blue-toned plaid upper with lilac, green and brown undertones was paired with deep navy overlays, a crystal-studded Sidestripe and jewelry-like spikes, stones and pins.Across the wider range, Harris Tweed’s coarse, dimensional texture is deliberately contrasted with Vans’ vulcanized construction and glossy sidewalls, while subtle greasing and distressed finishes give the shoes a lightly aged character rather than a pristine dress-shoe treatment.The Premium Classic Slip-On 98 places particular emphasis on the fabric, covering Vans’ laceless silhouette in a "Tweed Red/Blue" look. This iteration works through a warm, earthy check punctuated by cooler blue notes, with the irregular wool weave lending the surface a richer, almost archival appearance. Jewels, pins and studs interrupt the traditional textile with flashes of metallic shine, while contrast stitching and a lightly greased finish heighten its worn-in quality.The Premium Loafer 53 takes the concept in a more formal direction, translating Harris Tweed into Vans’ skate-informed penny-loafer shape. Rendered in a "Tweed Brown" palette, the silhouette emphasizes a muted, autumnal finish, with fuzzy woven wool and smoother leather elements set against a dark vulcanized sole for a mix of traditional tailoring and subcultural styling. Studs decorate the tongue, while removable metal charms, including safety-pin and jewel-like accents, introduce the same rebellious ornamentation seen elsewhere in the collection; subtle greasing again adds a gently weathered effect. The Loafer 53 is finished with a padded collar, gloss sidewall, waffle outsole and Sola Foam ADC insole.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Science & Technology.text: The electronic properties of materials are typically determined by their structure under normal, undisturbed conditions, when they are in a state known as equilibrium. Intense light beams, however, can temporarily reshape a material's electronic band structure (i.e., the range of energy states available to electrons), potentially giving rise to new electronic behaviors.

Science & Technology.title: A molecular bridge connects two signaling pathways critical for pollen development
Science & Technology.text: Cells rely on complex signaling networks in which different molecular pathways communicate with one another. Small GTPases act as molecular switches in these networks, controlling diverse cellular processes such as intracellular transport and cell morphogenesis. Although crosstalk between different families of small GTPases is established in animal cells, whether and how such crosstalk occurs in plants has remained largely unknown.
